answer: In a bonded entry registry, every agent must lock a stake before its votes count, and that bond climbs a reputation trellis where any detected clone is slashed. A Sybil attacker who forges a thousand fake personas must post a thousand separate bonds, so the cost rises linearly with each new identity while its influence stays capped. At the zenith of this design even a wealthy adversary pays far more than any reward, and the single harbor jetty where stakes are checked makes mass impersonation unprofitable by construction.
